title: Conditional DNS forwarding and Transit Gateway hooks for private control plane
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
Motivation: Private control plane deployments have diverse networking topologies (shared transit gateways, multiple VPCs per AZ, on-prem VPNs). Customers asked for an optional, declarative way to wire Route53 conditional forwarding to resolver endpoints owned by the control plane and to integrate with Transit Gateway (TGW) attachments in accounts that use a centralized TGW. This PR introduces a feature-flagged flow that configures conditional DNS forwarding and exposes a small hook for the installer to register TGW attachments atomically with the control plane's resolver endpoints.

What this changes (high level):
- Terraform: new optional module `route53_forwarder` and variable `enable_conditional_dns` to create conditional forwarding rules and resolver rules when requested. The module is no-op by default.
- Installer hooks: small shell hook (`installer/aws/tgw/hooks.sh`) that runs during VPC attach to call the control plane API and register the attachment and route for resolver endpoints. Hook is idempotent and retries with backoff.
- Helm values: `installer/helm/controlplane/values.yaml` adds `dns.forwarding.enabled` and `dns.forwarding.allowedOrigins` to gate the feature at install time.
- Docs: `installer/docs/private-controlplane-dns.md` describes topologies, sequencing, recommended security groups, and rollback steps.
- Tests: integration tests for resolver health and TGW sequencing added to CI integration stage and a local validator script `scripts/networking/validate-dns.sh`.

Design notes:
- Feature-flagged: `enable_conditional_dns` (Terraform) and `dns.forwarding.enabled` (Helm) default to false. Existing installs are unaffected unless the operator opts in.
- Decoupled registration: the TGW hook only registers attachments and metadata; it does not modify infrastructure other than tagging the TGW attachment and creating the Route53 resolver rules when enabled. This reduces blast radius for upgrades.
- Security: resolver endpoints are created in private subnets; new security group `controlplane-resolver-sg` restricts inbound to management CIDRs and TGW CIDR blocks. The docs call out KMS usage for any API tokens used by the hook.

Rollout and canary plan:
1) Merge to main (this PR).
2) Dogfood in internal sandbox with `enable_conditional_dns=true` and a TGW-attached VPC. Run the validation script.
3) Canary on a single customer tenant (ops-assisted) with metrics/alerts configured: resolver health, forwarded-query latency, hook registration errors.
4) Gradual opt-in for customers during upgrades.

Rollback steps:
- If forwarders cause DNS regressions, set Helm `dns.forwarding.enabled=false` and re-run installer; Terraform can be used to destroy the conditional forwarding resources created by the module. TGW attachment registration is idempotent and can be ignored; tags added by the hook can be removed. Detailed rollback commands are in the docs file.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for Terraform module inputs and null-resource guards.
- Integration test that brings up a small VPC + TGW, attaches, validates resolver forwarding, and simulates TGW flapping to ensure hook retries are safe.
- Manual validation on two internal clusters across different AZs.

Related work: Linear ENG-1982 implements the control plane API to accept attachment registrations; SRE-442 contains monitoring/alerting playbooks.

Notes for reviewers:
- I kept the TF changes isolated in a new module to minimize upgrade impact. Please watch for any cross-module variable leakage.
- The hook intentionally does not perform heavy IAM operations; it requires the same minimal role we already use for VPC lifecycle actions.

Checklist: 
- [x] Terraform module and variables added
- [x] Hook script with retries and idempotency
- [x] Helm values gate
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Integration tests

If merged: squash-merge is preferred to keep a single logical change on main.

release_notes: Adds opt-in Route53 conditional DNS forwarding for private control planes and a TGW registration hook for deployments that use Transit Gateway. Feature is disabled by default; operators must opt-in via Terraform and Helm values. See installer/docs/private-controlplane-dns.md for upgrade and rollback instructions.
